answer: No, as of today he doesn't need a notary in Virginia. The older guide on selling a family member's car says to use the notarized form NW-POA-1. However, on February 1, 2026, that form was replaced by power of attorney form NW-POA-2, which can be signed electronically with no notary. Only Georgia still requires a notary, so this doesn't apply to you in Virginia. An NW-POA-1 signed before February 1 was only accepted until June 30, 2026, so your dad should sign the new NW-POA-2. When you sell the car, bring the signed form, your own photo ID and the car's documents. Please note the power of attorney stops being valid if the person who signed it dies.
